message.content:
I don’t have live access to real‑time weather or pollution feeds, so I can’t give you an exact AQI (Air Quality Index) reading at this moment. However, here’s what you can do:

| Option | How it works |
|--------|--------------|
| **U.S. EPA AirNow** | Visit <https://www.airnow.gov/> and enter “Los Angeles” or your ZIP code. It will show the latest AQI values from nearby monitoring stations. |
| **Local news sites / apps** | Many city portals (e.g., L.A. Times, KABC) publish daily air‑quality updates on their websites or through mobile alerts. |
| **Weather services** | Apps like Weather.com, AccuWeather, or NOAA often include an AQI widget when you search for Los Angeles. |
| **Smartphone sensors** | Some phones come with built‑in particulate matter detectors (PM2.5/PM10). Check if yours has such a feature. |

If you’re planning outdoor activities today, look up the most recent AQI figure—values below 50 mean good conditions, while anything above 150 indicates unhealthy levels for sensitive groups.

Let me know if you'd like help interpreting those numbers!
message.reasoning: The user asks about current air quality in LA. We don't have real-time data; we can provide general info and suggest checking AirNow or local sources. No tool needed.
